question: 从1945年到2026年，全球所有核电站累计发生过多少次INES 4级及以上的核事故？请逐一列出每次事故的时间、地点、反应堆型号、事故等级、直接原因，以及事故后该国核电政策的具体变化（如立法、关停、新建冻结等）。对比这些事故前后5年内该国的核电发电量占比变化数据。
evaluation_note: 用于第4题评估。strict 表示严格应计入；lenient 表示宽松可接受。

items.name: Saint-Laurent A1
items.location: Saint-Laurent-des-Eaux nuclear power station, Loir-et-Cher, France
items.reactor_type: UNGG (uranium naturel graphite gaz / gas-cooled graphite-moderated reactor)
items.direct_cause: During refuelling, a graphite flow-control piece was mistakenly placed instead of a fuel element, partially blocking a CO2-cooled channel and melting 5 fuel elements.
items.policy_change: No national phase-out; France continued nuclear expansion but the Saint-Laurent accidents later reinforced abandonment of the UNGG line in favour of PWRs.
items.power_share_change: Open official series for exact 1964-1974 annual national nuclear shares were not found in one consistent source during this pass; use caution if a model gives precise annual percentages.

items.name: Bohunice A-1
items.reactor_type: KS-150 HWGCR (heavy-water moderated, CO2-cooled power reactor)
items.direct_cause: During refuelling, a fuel-loading error led to fuel damage and extensive contamination/corrosion; the serious 1977 event is described as INES 4 in Slovak INIS records.
items.policy_change: A-1 was permanently shut down; the programme shifted to Soviet VVER reactors.
items.power_share_change: National pre/post 5-year share figures were not resolved from a single official open series in this pass.

items.name: Three Mile Island Unit 2
items.direct_cause: Equipment malfunctions, design-related problems and worker errors; a stuck-open pilot-operated relief valve plus misleading instrumentation led operators to miss a loss-of-coolant accident and the core partially melted.
items.policy_change: NRC tightened oversight and made sweeping changes to emergency planning, operator training, human factors, inspections and plant design/equipment requirements.
items.power_share_change: The 5-year post-accident U.S. nuclear share rose rather than fell. Responses claiming a 1979-1984 decline are inconsistent with the EIA series.

items.name: Saint-Laurent A2
items.location: Saint-Laurent-des-Eaux nuclear power station, Loir-et-Cher, France
items.direct_cause: Corrosion caused attachments of an internal primary-circuit plate to fail; the plate was carried by the CO2 flow, blocked several channels, and melted 2 fuel elements (about 20 kg uranium).
items.policy_change: The reactor returned to operation in 1984, but the Saint-Laurent accidents are treated by ASN as part of the historical end of the UNGG line and transition to PWRs.
items.power_share_change: French official sources in this pass support the qualitative conclusion that nuclear share surged in the late 1970s and 1980s; a conflicting claim that the 5-year post-1980 share fell is not supported by the regulator history pages reviewed.

items.name: Chernobyl Unit 4
items.location: Chernobyl nuclear power plant, Ukraine (then USSR)
items.direct_cause: During an improper low-power test, safety measures were ignored; the reactor went out of control, exploded and burned. RBMK design weaknesses and lack of a containment structure aggravated the event.
items.policy_change: Internationally, the accident directly led to the 1986 Early Notification and Assistance Conventions. IAEA notes that all RBMK units were upgraded to eliminate the design deficiencies that contributed to the accident.
items.power_share_change: No single open official source with a clean USSR 1981-1991 annual nuclear-electricity-share series was verified in this pass. Models giving very precise percentages for the USSR should be treated cautiously unless they cite a primary statistical source.

items.name: Fukushima Daiichi
items.location: Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station, Japan
items.direct_cause: The earthquake and tsunami caused loss of off-site power and flooding that disabled emergency equipment, leading to prolonged station blackout, core damage and hydrogen explosions.
items.policy_change: Japan replaced the old regulator with the independent Nuclear Regulation Authority (NRA) and introduced more stringent regulatory requirements against extreme natural hazards and severe accidents.
items.power_share_change: Responses that broadly describe a collapse from roughly one-quarter/one-third of electricity to near zero are directionally correct; claims of 2016 still being around 5% are too high against the WDI/IEA series.

items.name: Fermi-1
items.ines_level: >=4 (retrospective classification used in secondary/IAEA-affiliated material; exact open regulator page with INES value not located in this pass)
items.direct_cause: A zirconium plate came loose and blocked sodium coolant flow to some fuel subassemblies; two subassemblies began to melt.
items.policy_change: The plant restarted later and was decommissioned in 1972. No clear nationwide U.S. nuclear policy reversal was identified from the official source reviewed.
items.power_share_change: Use only qualitative scoring unless a model cites a primary statistical source.

items.name: Lucens
items.reactor_type: HWGCR / heavy-water moderated, CO2-cooled experimental power reactor
items.ines_level: >=4 retrospective, but exact open official page with an unambiguous INES number was not located in this pass
items.direct_cause: A damaged constriction in the cooling circuit reduced coolant flow, causing overheating and melting of a fuel element, followed by pressure failure and limited radioactive release into the cavern.
items.policy_change: The accident ended the Lucens project; the plant was permanently shut down and later decommissioned.
items.power_share_change: Do not accept precise pre/post-5-year Swiss national share numbers unless the model cites a primary statistical source. Several model values conflict sharply.
